title: Mitigating Negative Transfer in Cross-Domain Recommendation via Knowledge Transferability Enhancement

problem.claim: Cross-domain recommendation can suffer from negative transfer when information from multiple source domains introduces harmful noise and irrelevant features into the target domain.

gap.claim: Existing methods give limited attention to negative transfer in multi-domain settings, and feature decomposition alone does not address all its causes.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes TrineCDR, a triple-level knowledge-transferability-enhanced model for multi-target cross-domain recommendation.
TrineCDR captures single-domain and targeted cross-domain embeddings and enhances transferability at the feature, interaction, and domain levels.
The model is evaluated for cross-domain recommendation under dual-target and multi-target scenarios using real-world Amazon and Douban datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: Unlike previous methods, TrineCDR models targeted cross-domain knowledge transfer and addresses three stated causes of negative transfer across feature, interaction, and domain levels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluation on real-world datasets sampled from Amazon and Douban in dual-target and multi-target scenarios.
The authors report that TrineCDR outperforms state-of-the-art cross-domain recommendation methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain recommendation is presented as a way to alleviate data sparsity through cross-domain knowledge transfer.
Negative transfer is underexplored in settings with numerous domains, where indiscriminate transfer introduces harmful noise and irrelevant features.
Existing feature-decomposition approaches do not capture all causes of negative transfer and are insufficient for multi-domain scenarios.
TrineCDR uses single-domain and targeted cross-domain embeddings and enhances transferability at feature, interaction, and domain levels.
The authors report evaluation on Amazon and Douban datasets and superiority over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract attributes negative transfer to multiple causes spanning feature, interaction, and domain levels.

interpretation.claim: Transfer mechanisms may need to control both what information is transferred and at which structural level it is transferred.

application.claim: For multi-domain transfer systems, evaluate and filter transferred knowledge at feature, interaction, and domain granularities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the same transfer controls are effective outside the reported recommendation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three causes of negative transfer in detail.
Dataset sizes, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or training procedure in detail.
